results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. The calyx is closest to the cortex and receives sensory interneuron afferents. The pedunculus is a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes. The mushroom body lobe system consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch, which have different structures at different life stages.

VFB holds [37](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of Kenyon cell") subclasses of [Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain").

results.response: The main input neurons to the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are sensory interneuron afferents to the calyx. VFB records show that there are [366](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body") neurons with presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body, including larval uniglomerular projection neurons and larval antennal lobe multiglomerular projection neurons. The connectome data indicates that these neurons provide input to the mushroom body.

results.question: What are the main components of the Drosophila central complex and what functions are they associated with?
results.response: The main components of the central complex are the ellipsoid body, fan-shaped body, paired noduli, asymmetrical bodies, and protocerebral bridge. These components are associated with functions including navigation and orientation, locomotor control, and sleep/arousal and memory-related behaviours.

results.response: The [lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111763 "Open lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2 in Virtual Fly Brain") is a type of neuron with a distinct dendritic arbor in each lobula plate layer, extending outwards from the main fiber in the direction of motion detection for the layer. It is involved in detecting looming stimuli and its activity elicits a jump escape response. The LPLC2 has its main dendritic arbors in layers 4 and 5B of the lobula, with minor processes in layer 5A, and presynaptic sites in layer 4. Its arbors span approximately 25 lobula optic columns, overlapping with other LPLC2 cells. The LPLC2 projects to an optic glomerulus of the PVLP, anterior to LPLC1 and dorsal to LC4. There are approximately 80 of these cells per optic lobe and they are cholinergic.

The downstream class-connectivity previews for adult thermosensory projection neurons include mushroom-body-associated dopaminergic neurons and gamma main Kenyon cells.

VFB records show that there are [366](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body") neurons with presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body and [304](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPostsynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with postsynaptic terminals in mushroom body") neurons with postsynaptic terminals in the mushroom body. The strongest specific targets of thermosensory neurons are projection neurons, adult antennal lobe projection neurons, and antennal lobe projection neurons, with 18.9, 18.8, and 18.7 synapses per connected pair, respectively. The strongest specific inputs to thermosensory neurons are [adult antennal lobe local neuron lLN2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007396 "Open adult antennal lobe local neuron lLN2 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [unilateral local interneuron of the adult antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00051503 "Open unilateral local interneuron of the adult antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [adult antennal lobe local neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007390 "Open adult antennal lobe local neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), with 10.1, 10, and 9.06 synapses per connected pair, respectively.

These connections suggest that thermosensory neurons may play a role in memory formation through their interactions with the mushroom body.

results.title: API: integrations
results.question: How do I explore Virtual Fly Brain neurons using Navis or pymaid?
results.response:
To explore Virtual Fly Brain neurons, you can use the following steps:
1. Connect to the VFB CATMAID server:
```
rm = pymaid.connect_catmaid(server="https://fafb.catmaid.virtualflybrain.org/", api_token=None, max_threads=10)
```
2. Retrieve neurons by ID:
```
n = pymaid.get_neurons(16)
```
3. Retrieve neurons by annotation:
```
bates = pymaid.find_neurons(annotations='Paper: Bates and Schlegel et al 2020')
```
4. Plot neurons with Navis:
```
navis.plot3d(n, width=1000, connectors=True, c='k')
```
5. Access neuron properties: `n.nodes`, `n.connectors`, etc.
6. Use pymaid to get connectivity data:
```
da1_ds = pymaid.get_partners(da1, threshold=3, directions=['outgoing'])
```
7. Use pymaid to get adjacency matrix:
```
adj = pymaid.adjacency_matrix(bates)
```
VFB's documentation does not appear to cover pymaid.
